svg.title: Maximum cross-sectional area occurs before maximum accumulated volume
svg.desc: A solid has radius two minus x centimetres for x from zero to two. The local disc area and volume derivative is pi times two minus k squared, largest at k zero with area four pi square centimetres and zero at k two. Accumulated volume is pi times four k minus two k squared plus k cubed over three. It increases from zero to its maximum eight pi over three cubic centimetres at k two. Every endpoint is included and filled. This derivative is per unit length, not per unit time.
